judge_edits.from: Der Lomi-Saft steht in der Sonne und reift in Glasgefäßen
judge_edits.to: Lomi-Saft, der in die Sonne kommt und in Glasgefäßen reift
judge_edits.why: The blind reader asked whether Jameed is the juice or a preserved product made from it ('Was dabei entsteht, heißt Jameed'). After the colon, 05 told a process about 'der Lomi-Saft', so Jameed and the juice stayed two things. The appositive 'Lomi-Saft, der ...' makes the juice itself the definition of Jameed: a liquid, as the ruling says. The verb is the same as in the FAQ ('kommt ... in die Sonne'), so one verbal form is used in the language. J3 is kept (in Glasgefäßen, which the source carries), J4 is kept (Saft in the sentence), and J5 is kept (no article before Jameed).

judge_edits.to: (so heißt der in der Sonne gereifte Lomi-Saft)
judge_edits.why: The reader flagged 'Brauch des „Jameed“ (der in der Sonne gereifte Lomi-Saft)' as equating a custom with a juice. That is a grammar fault: the nominative masculine gloss agrees with 'der Brauch', not with the genitive 'des „Jameed“'. With 'so heißt ...' the bracket says what the word Jameed names, which is the juice. The gloss was already published; only its link changes. Nothing is added, since en/ar carry no gloss here and the old gloss had no jars. The knowledge list ('das Trocknen an der Sonne und das Reifenlassen') stays per the brief, because it describes the fruit's craft.

judge_edits.from: Der Lomi-Saft steht in der Sonne, reift in Glasgefäßen und steht so das ganze Jahr über zur Verfügung
judge_edits.to: Der Lomi-Saft kommt in die Sonne, reift in Glasgefäßen und steht so das ganze Jahr über zur Verfügung
judge_edits.why: 05 brought in 'steht ... steht so zur Verfügung', two senses of one verb in a single clause. This edit makes the verb the same as the FAQ and lomi-body form ('kommt in die Sonne').

rulings.text: Jameed is a liquid: lime juice set in the sun and aged (owner ruling 2026-11-06). Use 'in der Sonne gereift(er)' for the adjective and 'kommt in die Sonne (und reift in Glasgefäßen)' for the verb. Never sonnengetrocknet / trocknet in der Sonne for the juice. 'Gereift' is natural for a matured liquid (gereifter Wein, gereifter Essig). The 'sun-ripened' reading the reader floated cannot attach to Saft, and the reader still answered 'liquid' (06 a).
'getrocknet' for the fruit (lomi-body, events) and 'das Trocknen an der Sonne' in the history-72 knowledge list stay. Both describe dried lomi, which is real (brief).

J2/J3/J4/J5 are respected. Limettensaft is used in the FAQ and fruits. Lomi-Saft is used in blog body, heading, history and events. Glasgefäße appear only where the source names them. Saft stands next to every Jameed. No der/das stands before Jameed.

blind_disposition.flag: [1] 'reift in der Sonne' for juice is odd
blind_disposition.why: 'Gereift' is the standard German word for an aged liquid. The reader's answer (a) still reads Jameed as a liquid matured in the sun. Drying is gone.

blind_disposition.flag: [2] 'das Trocknen an der Sonne' has no object
blind_disposition.why: The brief keeps the craft list as it stands. The object is the fruit, and the source list (التقليم والتشميس والتعتيق) is equally bare.

blind_disposition.flag: [5] Jameed: the juice or the preserved product?
[5] 'frisch, als Saft und getrocknet' conflicts with jameed
blind_disposition.why: Lomi is the named subject ('Verwendet wird die Lomi'). The sentence describes the fruit, mirroring ar «طازجاً وعصيراً ومجففاً».

blind_disposition.flag: [6] 'frisch, als Saft oder getrocknet' hard to parse
blind_disposition.why: This is pre-existing sentence structure, and the events line en is unchanged. Jameed is defined in the next sentence as juice.
